newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to review post-war fate of Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to review post-war fate of Nazi gold.

text.p: Responding to calls from congressmen and a Jewish group, the United States said on Friday it would study the "retrieval and disbursement" of Nazi gold and other assets after World War Two.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the study would look into what the U.S. government of the time knew about the dispersal of Nazi assets and U.S. contacts with the Swiss government at the time. The Nazis deposited vast amounts of valuables taken from Holocaust victims in Swiss banks.
Burns said the study of U.S. archives, to be carried out by State Department historians, would last several months and its results would be made public.

Republican Senator Alfonse D'Amato, chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, last month called for the State Department to investigate what he called "50 years of deception" by Switzerland over the amount of funds deposited by the Nazis.

Burns said his department was responding to requests by D'Amato and the World Jewish Congress about "what the U.S. government knew about the disposition of Nazi assets at that time (and) whether or not we had diplomatic contact with the Swiss government..."

Burns said there were unanswered questions about the roles of the U.S. and Swiss governments and the interaction between them. The State Department was treating this as a "highly urgent and priority matter."
